lines.cap: The richest woman in America wouldn't pay to heat her oatmeal. She ate it cold.
lines.say: The richest woman in America wouldn't pay to heat her oatmeal. She ate it cold.

lines.cap: Hetty Green. The late eighteen hundreds. She turned an inheritance into around a hundred million dollars, investing on Wall Street.
lines.say: Hetty Green. The late eighteen hundreds. She turned an inheritance into around a hundred million dollars, investing on Wall Street.

lines.cap: She wore the same black dress for years, until it fell apart. People called her the Witch of Wall Street.
lines.say: She wore the same black dress for years, until it fell apart. People called her the Witch of Wall Street.

lines.cap: She lived in cheap rented rooms, moving around to avoid taxes. Reportedly, she'd search her carriage for hours, for a lost two cent stamp.
lines.say: She lived in cheap rented rooms, moving around to avoid taxes. Reportedly, she'd search her carriage for hours, for a lost two cent stamp.

lines.cap: The dark part. When her son hurt his knee, the story goes, she took him to a free clinic for the poor, dressed in rags. The leg later had to be amputated.

lines.cap: When she died in 1916, she was one of the richest people in the world.
